cross_references.label: GOV Code §12955 (FEHA housing discrimination — substantive prohibition)
cross_references.description: §12989.2 provides the remedies for §12955 violations. The two provisions always operate together — §12955 defines the violation, §12989.2 defines what the court can award.

cross_references.label: Civ. Code §52 (Unruh Act remedies)
cross_references.description: §12955 violations by persons subject to §51 = per se §51 violation → §52 mandatory $4,000/offense statutory damages + actual damages + attorney's fees. The §52 track runs concurrently with §12989.2. The plaintiff takes the higher remedy or both where they don't overlap.

cross_references.label: Civ. Code §3294 (punitive damages)
cross_references.description: §3294 requires malice, fraud, or oppression showing for punitive damages. §12989.2 does not require this separate showing — a finding of discriminatory housing practice is sufficient. The distinction matters when pleading both §12955 claims and tort claims arising from the same transaction.

cross_references.label: 42 USC §3613 (FHA civil enforcement)
cross_references.description: Federal FHA civil action (§3613) runs parallel to FEHA §12989.1. FHA provides 2-year SOL, actual and punitive damages, attorney's fees. Both FEHA and FHA claims can be brought simultaneously in federal court. FETCH_REQUIRED for federal standard.
